statement: Agent-facing output is bounded and structured so one invocation cannot flood an agent context
description: Brief: agents hit APIs without clogging context. Large response bodies are truncated or summarized on agent paths; the exact bound is a later sharpening.

statement: Agents execute saved requests through the CLI in one non-interactive invocation that returns an exit status
description: From the brief's first consumer: agents are a first-class API client. No prompts, no TTY assumptions. The CLI surface is a contract agents can script against.

statement: Agent-facing output redacts credential material on every output path, and tokens are read from the environment at send time
description: Agents are first-class API clients: requests live in files, no token leakage, structured redacted output for postui run --json.

statement: Agents call real APIs through postui as a safe client that leaks no tokens and floods no context
description: Consumer 4 from the brief: your agents. The umbrella product promise for the agent surface; req_agent_exec, req_agent_bounded_output, req_agent_redaction, and req_env_tokens are its concrete guarantees.

statement: The CLI has exactly two output modes: human-pretty by default and --json validated against the schema contract
description: Current-state decision in the brief: postui <curl> pretty, postui --json machine-readable. The json path is the one gated by req_output_schema_gate.

statement: Any curl command a human pastes either parses to a structured request or fails with a named error, never a silent misparse
description: Brief: parse and display any curl, and the biggest engineering risk lives in curl parsing edge cases. This is the compatibility target the parser is held to.

statement: Unknown curl flags fail the parse. Recognized-but-ignored flags produce a warning and parsing continues
description: Error policy from src/curl/parse.ts behavior recorded in the brief.

statement: A parsed request is GET unless it carries a body, in which case it is POST
description: Method inference decision in src/curl/parse.ts; -X overrides.

statement: A curl invocation is the only authoring surface: requests are captured by hitting the API like a human, and tests, agents, and docs all read the same saved request files
description: Root product decision from the brief. No parallel collection format; the requests folder of executable TypeScript files is the single source of truth. The TUI browser over this workspace is deliberately last in the roadmap.

statement: Curl input is word-split per POSIX quoting rules — quotes, escapes, and line continuations — before any flag parsing
description: Decided in the brief's current-state notes: src/curl/shell.ts is a dedicated POSIX word splitter, not ad-hoc whitespace splitting.

statement: API documentation is produced from the same saved request folder, with no separate docs source
description: Consumer 3 from the brief's pitch: your docs read from the same folder. Undrawn: doc format and surface. This is the least-shaped consumer and the only one with no roadmap item yet.

statement: Saved request files reference credentials only as environment variable names resolved at send time
description: Brief: tokens come from env at send time. No credential material is ever stored in a request file. Complements req_agent_redaction, which covers output paths; this covers the files themselves.

statement: Test generators emit raw idiomatic code for the target framework, not output from an intermediate assertion language
description: vitest, bun:test, node:test first via one small emitter each; framework detected from package.json, flag overrides.

statement: A human pastes any curl and gets a readable, structured view of the request
description: Consumer 1 from the brief: you. postui <curl> pretty mode. The terminal is the inspection surface; this is the product promise the parsing layer serves.

statement: Serialized request output validates against the Effect Schema contract before it is emitted
description: Effect 3.22.1 Schema-validated JSON output on the --json path; Effect v4 stays out until stable (revisit decision recorded as fog).

statement: npm releases publish through OIDC trusted publishing with no long-lived tokens anywhere in the release path
description: release.yml on v* tags, id-token: write, npm environment gate, org staged-publishing as final approval.

statement: Integration tests for whichever framework the user runs are generated from the same saved requests
description: Consumer 2 from the brief: your tests. The product promise is generation from the shared workspace; req_gen_raw_emit governs the shape of what is emitted.

statement: Every failure is a typed Effect error (Data.TaggedError), never an ad-hoc thrown string
description: Key decision in the brief's table. Callers pattern-match on error types; exit codes derive from them.

statement: Saved requests are executable TypeScript files in the workspace folder — no .bru, no YAML DSL, no schema language
description: Format decision from the brief's why/non-goals sections.

statement: The request collection lives in the user repo as plain files, with no proprietary format and no collection database
description: Brief: the collection is a folder of plain TypeScript files, not a database. No collection index file, no proprietary format. Naming convention is a later decision.
